confidence_note: The Offer is described in the book: every new hire goes through a several-week training that includes time on the phones, and during it is offered money to quit. Hsieh writes that the amount started small and was raised over time, reaching $2,000 at the time of writing; the starting amount is left out. No take-up percentage is used. The supplied text's 'please do not take it' line is not presented as a quote.
facts: Every new Zappos hire, whatever the role, went through a training of several weeks that included answering customer calls.
During that training each new hire was offered money to quit on the spot.
The amount was raised over time and stood at $2,000 when Hsieh wrote the book.
The point was to find out early who wanted the job and the culture, and who was there only for the paycheck.
Hsieh's reasoning: someone who stays only for pay costs more over time than the offer does.
Most new hires did not take the money.
Turning it down made staying a choice the employee had made.
tension: A company spends weeks training people, then pays them to leave.
opening_idea: Start in the middle of the training, when the new hire is told they can walk out with $2,000.

lessons.idea: Commitment becomes real when leaving is easy and people stay anyway.
lessons.anchor: The Offer made in the middle of Zappos training.

reflect_final: What are you still doing mainly because leaving looks costly, and what would you choose if it were easy?

use_cases.situation: A team is discussing why some new hires disengage after a few months.
use_cases.move: Bring up Zappos paying people to quit during training, then ask how you could find out earlier who truly wants the role.

use_cases.situation: A new team member seems unsure about the job.
use_cases.move: Tell them it is fine to say early if this is not the right fit.

use_cases.situation: You stay in a commitment out of habit.
use_cases.move: Ask yourself whether you would sign up again today, and write the answer down.

pocket_idea: Zappos paid new hires to quit; when walking away is easy, the ones who stay have chosen to.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Zappos offered new hires $2,000 to quit in the middle of their training.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Every Zappos hire spent weeks in training, including on the phones, and was offered money to quit, $2,000 when Hsieh wrote the book. Most stayed, and staying became their own choice.
